scope: Follow-up to the first startup optimization, with the same frozen 512-match tournament response. Isolated Chrome; every server/write call simulated. No player data included.
behavior: For more than 50 finished matches, create lightweight row identities first. Only results selected by pagination, date expansion or search receive names, controls, cells and observers.
The complete model remains present and receives native score, full-match, metadata and name corrections. Search of finished games uses the model, including unrendered results.
Visible results are rendered from current model values on their original row objects. Already-rendered rows and player nodes remain reusable across pagination.
Date headings, sorting, counts, location filtering and the all-results preference continue to include every result. Opening more results creates no additional server requests.
Read tab geometry in one phase before writing navigation label widths, preserving the existing responsive rules.

comparison.baseline: Includes the previous main-display transaction, first-observation guard, timezone formatter cache and native name-measurement batching.
comparison.order: before, after, after, before; fresh Chrome sessions; no CPU profiler
comparison.measurement: Response handling after test-data preparation until three frames without pending tournament/board work. Asset/script loading and server latency excluded.

browser_runs.baseline_identical: Only row heights differ from historical expectation: 33.78125 vs 31 CSS pixels, identically before and after. Date states, counts, rows and player identities agree.

history_regressions.scope: Isolated browser with 150 synthetic results on two dates; pagination, search, updates, sorting, date expansion, row identity, unrendered score/name/metadata corrections, section changes, removal and reload persistence.
checks: The initial history retains all 150 results and displays 50 of the current day
Only the first 50 results have names, controls and cells at startup
Score, full-match, metadata and name updates retain an unrendered result without building cells
Searching a corrected hidden name builds only that result with its current score and metadata on the same row
Clearing search retains existing row and player nodes and leaves the other results unrendered
More results reveal the remaining current-day games on the same rows
The reduced view can be restored
Search finds a result beyond the initial page and from a collapsed day
Clearing search restores the reduced view
Opening another day reveals its first results instead of an empty group
A result updated outside the visible page retains its current score when shown
Sorting still includes all results
The all-results preference survives a page reload
Reopening an unrendered result removes its placeholder and creates one complete scheduled row
Finishing the reopened game shows the current result once without a stale placeholder
Removing an unrendered result removes its indexed placeholder
History pages leave no incomplete work or browser exceptions

installed_startup_smoke.scope: Synthetic isolated startup with 512 games and 423 finished.
checks: All 512 games and 50 visible results survive the initial build
The main view is visible after all startup work
A failed build restores prior inline display and priority
A complete rebuild recovers after failure with every game
No unexpected browser exceptions

limits: Two runs per variant on this machine. This is not a p99 latency guarantee for other devices.
Asset/script loading still requires approximately another half second locally. The full reload is not under one second.
Explicitly requesting all results or a broad search can still build all matching rows. Already-built rows remain allocated until leaving or rebuilding the view.
No backend, database, BTP write path or BUP client changes.
